questions.question: Electron-volt is a unit of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**energy.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The electron volt is the unit of **energy**__ commonly used in atomic and nuclear physics.

 __
 
• The amount of energy gained by the charge of a single electron moved across an electric potential difference of 1 volt is called an **electron volt.**
 
• It is commonly used in atomic and nuclear physics applications.
 
• The symbol of electron volt is **eV.**
 
• **1eV = 1.602×10-19 J**
 
• **1eV = 1.602 × 10−12 erg**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Other units of energy are:
 
 
• **Joule** is the SI unit of Energy.

 
 
• The unit Joule is named after the English physicist James Prescott Joule.
 
• Kg⋅m²⋅s⁻² is the SI base unit of Joule.
 
 
 
• **The calorie **is a unit of energy commonly used in nutrition.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Watt** is the SI unit of Power.

 
 
• The unit watt is named after scientist James Watt.
 
 
 
• **Volt** is the SI unit of potential difference.
 
• **Ampere** is the SI unit of current.

questions.question: The SI unit of magnetic flux is known as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Weber**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Unit of magnetic flux in the International System of Units (SI) is **Weber**.
 
• It is defined as the amount of flux that, linking an electrical circuit of one turn (one loop of wire), produces in it an electromotive force of one volt as the flux is reduced to zero at a uniform rate in one second.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Henry** is a unit of either **self-inductance **or **mutual inductance**, abbreviated **H**, and named for the American physicist Joseph Henry.

 
 
• One henry is the value of self-inductance in a closed circuit or coil in which one volt is produced by a variation of the inducing current of one ampere per second.
 
 
 
• **Femi **is a unit of length used to measure nuclear distances.
 
 
• 1 fermi = 10⁻¹⁵ meter.
 
• it was named for the Italian physicist **Enrico Fermi** (1901–1954).
 
• It is now obsolete, replaced by the SI term femtometer (symbol, fm).
 
• one fermi = one femtometer.

questions.question: Weber per second is equivalent to ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Volt.__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Weber per second** is equivalent to **Volt.**
 
• The SI unit of magnetic flux is Weber (Wb).

 
• Magnetic flux is a measurement of the total magnetic field which passes through a given area.
 
• Magnetic flux is the product of the average magnetic field times the perpendicular area that it penetrates.
 
• The SI unit of the magnetic field (B) is weber/meter2 (Wbm-2) or tesla.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__** 

 
• **Ampere - **It is the unit of **Electric Current**.
 
• **Volt - **It is the derived unit of **electric potential**.
 
• **Ohm - **It is the unit of** electrical resistance**.
 
• **Coulomb - **It is the SI unit of **electric charge.**

questions.question: Which one among the following measures the same quantity as that is measured by the SI unit ‘pascal’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tor**r__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **Torr** is a non-SI unit of pressure with a ratio of 760 to 1 standard atmosphere.
 
• It is defined as exactly 1/760 of a standard atmosphere (101325 Pa).
 
• Thus one torr is exactly 101325/760 pascals (≈ 133.32 Pa).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Joule**
 
 
 
• It is an SI unit of work or energy.
 
• It is equal to the work done by a force of one newton acting through one meter.
 
 
 
 

 **Newton**
 
 
 
• It is an SI unit of force.
 
• One newton is the force needed to accelerate one kilogram of mass at the rate of one meter per second squared in the direction of the applied force.
 
 
 
 

 **Watt**
 
 
 
• It is an SI unit of Power.
 
• It is equal to one joule of work performed per second, or to 1/746 horsepower.

questions.question: The SI unit of frequency is _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**hertz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **SI** unit of frequency is **hertz,** represented by the symbol **Hz**.
 
• It is named after a **German Physicist Heinrich Hertz **who** discovered** **electromagnetic radiation**.
 
• The **number of waves that pass a fixed point in unit time is called frequency** in other** words cycles per second is called frequency **before hertz it was measured in **cps cycles per second**.
 
• **1 Hz = 1 cps**
 
• Frequency is represented by the symbol **f**.
 
• **f=1/T (T represents time).****​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Volt **is the SI unit of **Potential Difference**.
 
• **Ohm **is the SI unit of **Electrical Resistance**.
 
• **Joule **is the SI unit of **Work and Energy**.

questions.question: What is the SI unit for measuring pressure?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pascal is the SI unit for measuring pressure**__.

 __
 
• The unit is named after Blaise Pascal, a French mathematician and physicist.
 
• 1 Pascal is equal to 1 Newton per Meter squared.
 
• In base units, 1 Pascal is equivalent to 1 kg⋅m−¹⋅s−².
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Candela** is the SI unit of luminous intensity.

 
 
• Luminous intensity is the quantity of visible light that is emitted in unit time per unit solid angle.
 
 
 
• **Kelvin** is the SI unit of temperature.
 
• **Ampere** is the SI unit of electric current.

questions.question: Which of the following is the physical quantity for the expression arc/radius?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** the Plane angle.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The physical quantity for the expression of arc/radius is the Plane angle.**
 
• A plane angle is well known: **one full revolution is 360° or 2π radians.**
 
• **Plane angle-** usually refers to an** angle in a 2-dimensional **figure like a** square, triangle, circle, etc.**
 
• **Solid angle **usually refers to an **angle in a 3-dimensional figure **like a cube, cuboid, sphere, etc.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Linear momentum**

 
 
• ​Linear momentum is the vector quantity and is defined as the product of the mass of an object, m, and its velocity, v. 
 
• The linear momentum formula is given by, **P = m v,** where m=mass, v= velocity.
 
• The units of linear momentum are** kg m/s.**
 
 
 
• **Surface tension​**
 
 
• ​Surface tension can be defined as **the property of the surface of a liquid that allows it to resist an external force, due to the cohesive nature of the water molecules.**
 
• Surface tension,** represented by the symbol γ** (alternatively σ or T), is measured in** force per unit length.**
 
• Its **SI unit is newton per meter and** the** cgs unit of dyne per centimetre.**
 
 
 
• **​Velocity**
 
 
• **​Velocity (v) is a vector quantity** that measures** displacement (or change in position, Δs) over the change in time (Δt).**
 
• Velocity is represented by the equation **v = Δs/Δt.**

questions.question: What is the SI unit of mutual inductance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Henry**__.

__
 
• Henry is the SI unit of mutual inductance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Mutual Inductance is the interaction of one coil's magnetic field on another coil as it induces a voltage in the adjacent coil.
 
• It is the basic operating principle of the transformer, motors, generators, and many other electrical components that interact with another magnetic field. 
 
• The mutual inductance between the two coils can be greatly increased by **positioning them on a common soft iron core** or by **increasing the number of turns**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weber **is the SI unit of m**agnetic flux.**
 
• **Farad **is the SI unit of **electrical capacitance.**
 
• Tesla (T) is SI unit of magnetic flux density or magnetic field strength.

• Energy is measured as the capacity to do work.
 
• It is a scalar quantity.
 
• Its SI unit is **Joule** and CGS unit is** Erg.**
 
• There are different forms of energy:
 
 

 
• Heat Energy: It is the energy by a body due to its temperature.
 
• Internal Energy: The total energy possessed by a body by virtue of the particular configuration of its molecules and also their random motion is called internal energy.

• Chemical Energy: The energy absorbed or released during a chemical reaction is called chemical energy.
 
• Nuclear Energy: The energy absorbed or released during a nuclear reaction is called nuclear energy.

__**Momentum:**__

__
 
• Momentum is the product of the mass of an object and the velocity it is moving with.
 
• Hence SI unit of momentum is the product of SI units of mass and Velocity.

• SI Unit of Velocity = Meter per Second (m/s).
 
 
• **So, SI Unit of Momentum = Kg m/s.**
 
 
 
• The dimensional formula for momentum is MLT⁻¹.

questions.question: Which one of the following element is Monatomic unit?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gold**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gold is a Monatomic unit**__.

 __
 
• Monatomic elements are elements that are stable as single atoms.
 
• For an element to be stable by itself, it must have a stable byte of valence electrons.
 
• The atomic number of a monoatomic element is equal to the number of protons in the element.
 
 
 
• Under standard temperature and pressure conditions, the monatomic elements are the noble gases helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, and radon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gold is the most malleable and ductile metal.**

 
 
• **Symbol: Au**
 
• **Atomic no.: 79**
 
• It is a soft metal and is usually alloyed to give it more strength.
 
• It is a good conductor of heat and electricity and is unaffected by air and most reagents.
 
• The most common gold compounds are auric chloride (AuCl₃) and chloroauric acid (HAuCl₄).

questions.question: The unit of calorific value of a fuel is expressed as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**kJ/kg**__.

__
 
• We know that **when the fuel is burnt** **heat is produced**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **The amount **of **heat that different types of fuels produced** on burning are expressed in terms of **calorific value**. 
 
• Thus **Calorific value **of a fuel is the amount of heat produced when **1 gm of fuel is completely burne**d.
 
• **S.I. unit of calorific value of fuels** is **kilojoule per kilogram (KJ/kg)**.
 
• It is calculated by **keeping the pressure constant** and in **normal temperature conditions**.
 
• It is also called **calorific power**. 
 
• For example, **if burning completely one kilogram of wood produces 17 kilojoules of heat, therefore, the calorific value of wood will be 17 KJ/kg.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• psi: Pounds per square inch (pressure)
 
• micron: Micrometer (length)
 
• mmHg: Millimeters of mercury (pressure)
 
• kJ/kg: Kilojoules per kilogram (specific energy)

questions.question: What is the power of ‘second’ in the SI unit of acceleration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**-2.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The **SI unit of acceleration** is **meters/second² (m/s²). **
 
• **Hence, the power of the second is -2 as it is in the denominator.**
 
• Acceleration (a) is defined as the** rate of change in velocity. **
 
• **Velocity is a vector quantity**, and therefore **acceleration is also a vector quantity. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Types of acceleration**
 
• **Uniform acceleration**
 
 
• When an object is travelling in a straight line with an increase in velocity at equal intervals of time, then the object is said to be in uniform acceleration. The free-falling of an object is an example of uniform acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Non-uniform acceleration**
 
 
• When an object is travelling with an increase in velocity but not at equal intervals of time is known as non-uniform acceleration. Bus moving or leaving from the bus stop is an example of non-uniform acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Instantaneous acceleration**
 
 
• The acceleration of an object at any instant of time is known as instantaneous acceleration.

questions.question: Farad is the unit of _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**capacitance**__.

__
 
• Farad is the unit of capacitance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• Capacitance is the property of an electric conductor measured by the amount of separated electric charge that can be stored on it per unit change in electrical potential.
 
• It is given by-
 
• ** C = {qover V}.**
 
 
• Where, C= Capacitance, q=amount of charge, V=potential difference between the conductors.
 
 
 
• Capacitance in electric circuits is introduced by a device called a **capacitor**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Weber **is the unit of Magnetic flux.
 
• **The reciprocal of resistance **of a conductor is called its **conductance**.
 
 
• Its SI unit is ohm⁻¹.
 
 
 
• The magnetic flux density of a point in a** magnetic field is the force experienced by a north pole of unit strength placed at that point. **
 
 
• Its SI unit is **Newton/ampere-metre Weber/meter² (Wb/m²) or 1 tesla (T).**

questions.question: The SI unit of power of lens is ____________.
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct, i.e. __**Dioptre**__.

__
 
• **Dioptre__ is the S.I. Unit of Power of a lens**.
 
• A dioptre is equal to the reciprocal of the focal length measured in meters.
 
• The Power of a lens is the ability of a lens to converge or diverge light rays depending on its focal length.
 
• The power of the lens is** the ability of the lens to converge the rays of light falling on it**. Definition: The power of a lens** is the reciprocal of its focal length in meters**.
 
• When, f = 1 m, P = 1/f = 1/1 = 1 dioptre. 1 dioptre is the power of a lens whose focal length is **1 meter**.
